statusGroups.reason: The C# static projection implements fifteen raster, nearest-point, polygon, triangulation, atlas and intersection methods. Polygon boolean/offset, convex decomposition and other reference methods remain absent; see docs/classes/Geometry.md.

Fifteen stateless methods follow the pinned formulas and typed result adaptation; GeometryTests covers boundaries, degenerate inputs, winding, hull, both triangulation methods, atlas layout, crossing and null cases on Linux/.NET 8. CanvasPolygonTests covers renderer reuse and zero-allocation redraw. Native and exhaustive numeric parity remain unverified.

All 146 named values were compared with pinned XML; constructors, methods, properties and operators were audited against pinned XML, typed C# formulas, the existing ADR 0024 native-source audit and VerifyColors. Integer scalar calls use C# int-to-float conversion; Color8(byte) follows the accepted typed C# channel range (ADR 0024). Clamping, defaults, rounding and managed failures follow ADRs 0024/0034. Verified on Linux/.NET 8; no native ABI or cross-platform claim.

All 82 members were audited against pinned XML, native formulas and typed C# value operators. VerifyVector2Values covers values, defaults, arithmetic, geometry and managed failure boundaries; ADRs 0033/0034 record typed C# differences including midpoint-to-even Round. Verified on Linux/.NET 8 only.

All 43 members were audited against pinned XML, native formulas and typed C# operators. VerifyTransforms covers values, defaults, algebra, errors and arrays; ADRs 0029/0034 record C# adaptations. Verified on Linux/.NET 8 only.

All 53 members are accounted for and behavior-audited. Squared norms use signed 64-bit results with a checked C# boundary; ordinary lengths remain finite across all 32-bit coordinates (ADR 0033). Boolean truth conversion is excluded by ADR 0001.
Values match the pinned XML and Vector2I properties; layout and constants are checked by VerifyVector2IValues.
The zero-initialized and copied C# struct preserves both components; the two-int constructor and mutable fields are checked by VerifyVector2IValues.
Both axes are present with X=0 and Y=1, matching the pinned enum and MaxAxisIndex/MinAxisIndex results.
Componentwise absolute value matches the reference for representable values; int.MinValue throws OverflowException as a documented managed boundary.
X divided by floating-point Y matches the reference, including IEEE results when Y is zero.
Componentwise clamping matches the pinned XML and managed binding; reversed bounds throw ArgumentException under the typed C# contract.

Components widen before multiplication and the result is exact signed 64-bit within range: (50000, 0) yields 2500000000. Results above long.MaxValue throw OverflowException as the ADR 0033 typed C# boundary.

Coordinate differences widen before subtraction, then square into an exact signed 64-bit result within range. Results above long.MaxValue throw OverflowException; this avoids native int32 subtraction overflow (ADR 0033).
Widened floating-point squares produce a finite single-precision length over the full int32 component range, including when the signed 64-bit squared API reaches its checked limit (ADR 0033).
Widened coordinate differences and floating-point squares produce a finite single-precision distance over the full int32 range, avoiding native int32 subtraction overflow (ADR 0033).
Componentwise integer min/max agrees with the pinned methods and is exercised by VerifyVector2IValues.
X wins maximum ties and Y wins minimum ties, matching the pinned reference and boundary tests.
Each component becomes -1, 0, or 1 as in the pinned reference; negative and zero components are tested.
Each component follows floor(value/step + 0.5) * step, including negative steps and zero-step preservation; checked overflow is a documented C# safety boundary.
Componentwise equality and lexicographic X-then-Y ordering match the pinned operators and are exercised by VerifyVector2IValues.
The vector/int operators use componentwise 32-bit arithmetic and C# truncated division/remainder; wrapping and invalid division are documented managed adaptations and have boundary tests.
The float overload returns Vector2 and performs componentwise IEEE 754 multiplication, as documented in the typed vector contract (ADR 0033).

The float overload returns Vector2 and performs componentwise IEEE 754 division, including infinity or NaN for a zero divisor; ADR 0033 accepts this typed result in place of a dynamic Variant error state excluded by ADR 0001.
C# indexer reads or writes X/Y for indices 0/1 and rejects other indices with ArgumentOutOfRangeException, a documented managed safety boundary.
Unary plus returns the same value, including both components.
The Vector2-to-Vector2I constructor truncates finite in-range components toward zero; rejecting nonfinite/out-of-range input is the accepted typed C# safety rule in ADR 0033.

Sibling norm implementation widens before multiplication and distance subtraction; squared results return exact signed 64-bit values or throw above long.MaxValue, while ordinary length/distance remain finite across the int32 range (ADR 0033).

Executable native PNG/JPEG/WebP/BMP/TGA loading and PNG/JPEG saving with file/buffer paths, RGBA8 copied base pixels, size preflight, atomic replacement and Linux x64 tests in ImageCodecTests; decoded PNG texture output verified on Wayland/Vulkan. Original channel layouts, color/profile metadata, full codec variants, additional Load formats and AOT remain unaudited or unfinished. See docs/classes/Image.md and ADR 0039.

The authorized SDL_image 3.4.6 encoder at quality 100 changes opaque colors in a lossless round trip. Native encoder correction with exact color/alpha verification is required before the public lossless/lossy WebP save contract can be exposed (ADR 0039); no additional package was selected.

Scalar curve API audited against pinned source and XML: sorted/clamped insertion, Free/Linear slopes, domain/value constraints, exact/cached samples, resolution-one behavior, typed indexed descriptors and synchronous notification timing. CurveTests verifies analytic values, edits, duplicate cleanup, tangent refresh, finite-domain cache arithmetic, copying, PackedScene ownership, callback/disposal failures, concurrency and warm allocation. ADRs 0013/0034 record typed exceptions, canonical epsilon and proven cleanup/tangent/overflow corrections; no Variant storage or native dependency. See docs/classes/Curve.md.

PathCurve implements the spatial curve resource under ADRs 0004/0013: relative handles, segment/fraction samples, distance/tangent caching, cubic/linear baked queries, closest projection and both tessellations. CurveTests verifies analytic and degenerate geometry, closed segments, cache failure recovery, copies, typed descriptors, scene-local ownership, callbacks, concurrency and warm allocation. ADR 0013 records closed-segment and zero-length corrections, finite-input exceptions and bounded 0..20 subdivision depth; default cache depth is ten. No native backend is needed. See docs/classes/PathCurve.md.

The complete declared RNG surface is executable: pinned PCG32 vectors, state replay, range boundaries, weighted errors/selection, normal sampling and managed lifetime are checked by RandomNumberGeneratorTests. Time-dependent seeds and C# unsigned/typed-array representation are accepted adaptations; other platforms remain unverified under ADR 0021.

The complete declared bit mask contract is executable: alpha thresholding, bit operations, nearest resize, L8 image conversion, circular dilation/erosion, marching-squares contours, resource copying and lifetime have managed tests. Native platforms beyond Linux remain unverified.
